title: clauses-prioritization-preflight-list
content:
Purpose: quick personal preflight before a negotiation call. Compact checklist that reminds me which clauses to anchor, which to trade, and what scripts to use. Intended as a one-pager scratchpad to carry into a negotiation and to paste into an internal Slack thread after the call.

High-level objectives (one line each):
- Protect customer data residency and export rights where required.
- Keep liability cap within 3x committed ARR for commercial deals; carve out willful misconduct and IP indemnity.
- Ensure operational SLAs that map to obvious remedies (credits, rollback, fallback).
- Avoid broad audit rights that allow unlimited data extraction or live system access.

Priority ranking (Must-win / Tradeable / Nice-to-have):
1) Must-win: Data residency & export controls (explicit region commitments), Encryption key control for Private deployments (bring-your-own-key allowed), Termination data export window and format (30 days minimum).
2) Tradeable: Subprocessor list and notice period (we can accept 30-day rolling notification + category list, oppose unlimited subcontracting), SLA response/availability numbers (we can accept slightly higher latency SLO for heavy bursts if credits are meaningful).
3) Nice-to-have: Escrow of last-known-good model weights (ask, but accept alternative: guaranteed rollback + model artifact hashes), On-prem deployment timeline guarantees.

Clauses to watch (quick red flags):
- Broad indemnities covering downstream customer outputs (push back: limited to direct damages caused by Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct).
- Unlimited audit rights or rights to copy production data (ask for scoping and frequency limits; require encrypted, read-only logs for audits).
- Termination for convenience with no transition assistance (must require export support and contact person for 30/60-day window).
- Language that makes model outputs Redwood IP regardless of customer prompts/data (clarify ownership of customer prompts/data and customer ownership of outputs).

Sample anchor language (short snippets I prefer to paste in emails):
- Data residency: "Redwood will store and process Customer Data in the Customer's selected region(s) and will not export Customer Data outside those regions except as required by law; Customer will be notified 30 days in advance of any planned cross-border processing."
- Key control: "For Private deployments, Customer may provide and rotate encryption keys using their KMS. Redwood will have no persistent access to unencrypted keys."
- Termination transition: "Upon termination, Redwood will provide Customer with a machine-readable export of Customer Data and associated metadata in NDJSON or parquet within 30 days, and will securely delete remaining copies per agreed schedule."
- Liability cap: "Except for liabilities arising from willful misconduct, gross negligence, or IP indemnities, Redwood's aggregate liability will be limited to the greater of $500,000 or 3x Customer's 12-month fees paid to Redwood preceding the event."

Negotiation scripts / soundbites (short, use on calls):
- "We understand you want broad auditability — can we scope that to compliance-related audits no more than once per year, with advance notice and mutually agreed format?"
- "On export: we can commit to the selected region(s) for production data. If you have regulatory requirements for on-prem, we can prioritize the private deployment track and agree on milestones."
- "For liability, our ask is parity: we have obligations to partners and a cap that keeps us able to operate. Let's find a middle ground that addresses your risk without removing our ability to deliver."

Concession ladder (what to give up, in order):
1) Extend notice windows (30 -> 45 days) for subprocessors.
2) Accept a narrower SLA credit formula if the credit is meaningful and automatically applied.
3) Commit to an accelerated private deploy timeline only for committed Dedicated deals (with fees).

Escalation triggers (raise to GC / Sales lead):
- Customer insists on uncapped liability for non-IP harms.
- Demand for raw data export without redaction or secure transfer protocols.
- Requirement to host keys on vendor-managed HSM without technical justification.

Practical redline tactics:
- Replace absolute words: "will" -> "will use commercially reasonable efforts to" only where appropriate (but avoid weasel-phrases on core promises like region commitments).
- Add explicit success metrics for anything with a remediation (e.g., SLA uptime number + credit calculation).
- Add time-boxed obligations for audits and export (frequency, format, recipient).

Open questions to resolve before final sign: (assign owner)
- Who will manage KMS integration on the customer's side? (owner: Solutions Eng)
- If the customer demands model escrow, what is the minimal acceptable artifact set (weights, tokenizer, config)? (owner: Applied ML)
- Acceptable audit vendor list and redaction process? (owner: Security)

Post-call follow-ups (copy/paste checklist):
- Summarize agreed redlines in an email with bullets and proposed language.
- Upload the redlines to JIRA under contract-review ticket and link to this doc.
- Flag any GC-level escalations and book 30-min sync with GC + Sales if escalation triggers hit.

Quick templates (email snippets):
- "Thanks — per our call, attached proposed language for data residency and key control. If that aligns, we'll ingest into the next draft and share for your review by EOD Thursday."
- "For SLA credits: propose automatic offset equal to coinsurance of 5% monthly fees for each 0.5% below target up to 25% cap. Happy to model this for a sample month."

Notes to self (do not send):
- Remember: contracts are negotiation leverage for sales. Protect product constraints (e.g., we cannot promise geographic affinity for ephemeral caching without engineering signoff).
- Keep the ask simple: prefer clear black-letter language over long procedural appendices.

Revision history (personal):
- 2025-08-19: initial draft with clause list and anchor language.
- 2025-09-02: added escalation triggers and post-call checklist.

End of scratchpad.
